svg.aria-label: How to write ഠ: one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing ഠ
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ഠ (malayalam), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansMalayalam-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Sachin Nandakumar, Jayasree: Malayalam handwriting, animated stroke by stroke (github.com/sachn1/jayasree, commit e0c9d57, October 2026), js/src/stroke-data.raw.json: the hand-recorded centre-line stroke for ഠ; "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, CC BY 4.0 <https://github.com/sachn1/jayasree/blob/e0c9d57dd32031c948da4d5f8432aae3e22c5bba/js/src/stroke-data.raw.json>. Source note on variation: Jayasree records ഠ as one stroke that starts at the top of the ring and runs anticlockwise: down the left side first, round the bottom, up the right side and closed at the top. The sources disagree on the direction. SPACE Kerala's Thooval (GPL-3.0, facts only) and the grahyam samples (no licence, counts only) were read in an earlier round as anticlockwise too, while Moag's Table IV arrow (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, facts only) runs the ring clockwise; Jayasree breaks that tie, three sources to one, and a learner taught the clockwise ring is not wrong. Jayasree keeps one recorded gesture per pen-down stroke, so one stroke means the recorder did not lift. Only these facts (stroke count, start, order, direction and end) are taken; no recorded coordinate is copied. The stroke data is licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) as "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, https://github.com/sachn1/jayasree; this record adapts it, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to the recording, which was drawn over the Manjari typeface. One recorder, so confidence is medium.
